hints: Identify all energy changes for the block descending $2\text{ m}$ along the plane inclined at $30^\circ$: initial kinetic energy, loss in gravitational potential energy, work done against resistance, and final kinetic energy.
Calculate the vertical drop $h = 2 \sin 30^\circ = 1\text{ m}$ to determine the loss in potential energy: $\Delta PE = mgh = 20(10)(1) = 200\text{ J}$.
Apply the work-energy equation $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 - \frac{1}{2}mu^2 = \Delta PE - W_{\text{resistance}}$ and solve for the final speed $v$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy over a distance of $2\text{ m}$ down the $30^\circ$ incline:
$$\Delta PE = mg(s \sin 30^\circ) = 20 \times 10 \times (2 \sin 30^\circ) = 200 \times 1 = 200\text{ J}$$

Form the work-energy relation with initial speed $u = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and work against resistance $W_R = 50\text{ J}$:
$$\frac{1}{2}m v^2 - \frac{1}{2}m u^2 = \Delta PE - W_R$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(20)v^2 - \frac{1}{2}(20)(5^2) = 200 - 50$$
$$10v^2 - 10(25) = 150 \implies 10v^2 - 250 = 150$$

Solve for the final speed $v$:
$$10v^2 = 400 \implies v^2 = 40 \implies v = \sqrt{40} \approx 6.32\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Apply the work-energy principle for motion along a rough plane:
$$\text{Final Kinetic Energy} = \text{Initial Kinetic Energy} + \text{Potential Energy Lost} - \text{Work Against Resistance}$$
$$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2}mu^2 + mgh - W_R$$

Step 1: Calculate the initial kinetic energy with mass $m = 20\text{ kg}$ and initial projection speed $u = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$KE_{\text{initial}} = \frac{1}{2}(20)(5^2) = 10 \times 25 = 250\text{ J}$$

Step 2: Calculate the vertical drop $h$ as the block slides a distance $s = 2\text{ m}$ down an incline of $30^\circ$:
$$h = s \sin 30^\circ = 2 \times \frac{1}{2} = 1\text{ m}$$
The loss in gravitational potential energy is:
$$\Delta PE = mgh = 20 \times 10 \times 1 = 200\text{ J}$$
Step 3: The work done against the resistance force is given directly as $W_R = 50\text{ J}$.

Step 4: Substitute all quantities into the work-energy equation:
$$\frac{1}{2}(20)v^2 = 250 + 200 - 50$$
$$10v^2 = 400$$

Step 6: Take the positive square root to determine the speed:
$$v = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10} \approx 6.32456\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 6.32\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
